scope: Read-only API seam advisory answering only the R14 O_RDWR gap, the R6 flat output-limit projection against the full three-group foundation limits, and the minimal private error facade. No source, test, build, Git, lease, process, model, UI, provider, network, kernel, or legacy changes.

od_rdwr_gap.finding: R6 requires the private temp to have read/write access and requires exact same-descriptor payload rereads before link and during final verification. R14 lists O_RDONLY and O_WRONLY but omits O_RDWR from its capability preflight.
required_contract: Require an integer os.O_RDWR capability in the per-session snapshot; it must be a usable nonzero protection flag, just as the other access flags are checked.

Open the owned temporary with O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC and the retained parent dir_fd. Keep that one descriptor for bounded writes, seek/read exact-payload checks, fstat and cleanup.

Keep O_RDONLY for retained resources, metadata and raw inputs. O_WRONLY is not a substitute for the temp because it cannot support the required same-descriptor readback; do not silently open a second path-based or independent read descriptor.
Classify a missing or unusable O_RDWR primitive as unavailable_primitive before output creation, using the existing R8 I/O detail and final-verification precedence.
od_rdwr_gap.consequence: Until O_RDWR is named and tested, R14 does not fully prove the R6/R8 installer contract on a path that writes and then rereads the same temporary inode.

foundation_input_and_result.shape: Independent plain nested map with exactly git, config and public groups; caller input is the complete three-group map or the private omission sentinel None.

mapping.max_bundle_bytes: materialized["public"]["max_bundle_bytes"] -> retained manifest and byte-identical bundle.json saved bytes
mapping.max_output_peak_bytes: materialized["public"]["max_output_peak_bytes"] -> retained logical bytes plus the concrete installer peak

set_output_limits_flat.validation: The session receives a fresh exact builtin flat dict, validates the seven-key set and positive values within the corresponding hard maxima, copies it, and permits one narrowing only. It rejects nested groups, admission keys, semantic-only keys, extra keys, missing keys, bools, nonpositive values and later widening.

excluded_by_design.max_inline_normalized_bytes: Semantic normalized-target input bound; enforce during public preflight from the full public group before session installation, not in the filesystem output setter.
excluded_by_design.admission_caps: Fixed raw request/observe reader caps; they are not materialized request limits and are enforced before JSON decoding.
excluded_by_design.config_group: Consumed by the pure configuration parser and derivation; it is not an output-layout map.
excluded_by_design.git_group: Consumed separately by pure Git validation and raw-body retention; it is not an output-layout map.

git_projection.retain_bundle_bodies_argument: Pass a fresh exact five-key materialized["git"] projection, preserving max_targets, max_objects, max_tree_entries, max_object_bytes and max_total_object_bytes.
git_projection.rule: The retained body reader must enforce the lowered per-object and aggregate byte caps before/while bounded reads. The pure Git kernel still receives all five lowered Git limits and keeps its own frozen codes/details; do not flatten Git keys into set_output_limits or silently substitute profile hard bytecaps.

ordering_and_budget: Materialize and validate the complete nested limits map before any new intent write.
Run semantic validation, saved-envelope serialization and all deterministic output-peak simulation from the nested map.

Project the seven output keys once into set_output_limits before the first install; current retained bytes and each missing payload must use the lowered max_output_peak_bytes with R9 C+2*N accounting.
Keep raw body retention on the separate five-key Git projection and preserve lowered max_object_bytes/max_total_object_bytes independently of output caps.
limits_seam.consequence: This preserves the full3group foundation contract, makes the R6 setter exact and non-ambiguous, and prevents either max_inline_normalized_bytes or lowered Git bytecaps from disappearing during orchestration.

private_surface.io_failure: One private retained-I/O failure record carrying a frozen public code plus the exact nine-field R8 detail object; no raw exception/path/parser text and no public envelope construction inside the I/O graph.
private_surface.resource_failure: Use the foundation CodeProofResourceError with only reason in resource_origin/resource_hash/resource_shape and its fixed safe message; the retained-I/O adapter maps it to CODE_PROOF_RESOURCE_INVALID with the R8 detail shape when the initial resource state remains unchanged.
private_surface.structure_failure: Use CodeProofStructureError with only type/shape/limits and its fixed safe message; the public orchestrator maps it after strict input parsing to its existing bounded semantic context, normally CODE_PROOF_DOCUMENT_INVALID with a known pointer/reason.
private_surface.active_session_misuse: Keep RuntimeError("CODE session is not active") private for before-yield/finalizing/after-close wrapper misuse; it is not a wire or CLI error.

r8_detail_exact_shape.failed_groups: unique fixed-order group tokens, at most eight

public_code_mapping: WORK_PATH_UNSAFE wins whenever a retained edge, stamp, byte set or complete set persistently changes or becomes uncheckable, regardless of the earlier semantic, limit, resource, operation or cleanup error.
If no lineage failure exists, a cleanup I/O failure outranks the original operation error; otherwise preserve the original bounded operation error.
Use CODE_PROOF_BUSY for the nonblocking checkout-lock contention context and CODE_PROOF_IO_ERROR for ordinary retained I/O/unavailable-primitive failures, both with exit code 2.
Use CODE_PROOF_RESOURCE_INVALID for unchanged initial resource missing/type/mode/link/hash/shape/origin outcomes, represented through the R8 detail fields and R9 extended reason set.

Keep CODE_PROOF_LIMIT_EXCEEDED details exactly {instance_pointer, limit_name, limit, observed}; keep CODE_PROOF_CONFLICT exactly {instance_pointer, reason}. Do not wrap either in the R8 I/O detail or change their contexts.
Propagate frozen pure Git/config kernel error codes and details unchanged when no retained-lineage failure overrides them.
private_error_facade.cli_compatibility: At the command boundary, adapt the selected private code/details into the existing CLI error envelope and renderer. Do not add a new outer error schema, alter legacy commands, change the Git/config kernels, or route through legacy path/resource loaders. Private safe messages remain fixed and source-free; suppress raw exception chaining.

bounded_conclusion: Amend the next I/O freeze with O_RDWR and same-descriptor temporary readback requirements.
Freeze set_output_limits as the exact seven-key public output projection, retaining full nested limits above it and a separate full five-key Git projection for body/kernel paths.
Use one private R8-shaped retained-I/O adapter plus the existing foundation private resource/structure errors and existing CLI envelope mapping.
